Subject: Cross-cloud inference compare: post-call recap & next lab steps

Team — quick recap from this morning's discovery with YottaHost (Alex/Samir + CloudOps):

TL;DR
- They ran a handful of hyperscaler tests and see a widening p95/p99 gap at long contexts (>2k tokens) and during microburst concurrency.
- Primary asks: 1) reproducible head-to-head p95/p99 + tokens/sec; 2) a short A/B run we can hand them for procurement (latency vs cost); 3) a clear list of differentiators for the SRE/procurement review.

Key notes from call:
- Workloads: mostly conversational agents with ~1.5–4k token contexts; lots of short interactive requests mixed with occasional long completions.
- Failure modes: long-tail p99 spikes during cache misses and when batching is forced by high concurrency.
- Comparison targets: GCP AI + Azure OpenAI public endpoints (they will share current test artifacts).
- Procurement timeline: they need a short lab readout and initial numbers for SOW/SA by week of 7/26.

Proposed immediate plan (owners):
1) Test harness & measurement spec — Marissa to finalize the run matrix and p95/p99 probe spec (see attached p95-p99-probe-spec.md).
2) Instance provisioning & reproducible infra — Ben to provision temporary staging pools (Redwood Dedicated-style configs + equivalent hyperscaler instances). Attach: yottahost-capacity-matrix.xlsx for initial sizing.
3) Tracing & artifacts — Jordan to add trace IDs, sample curl reproducers, and a minimal dataset (seed prompts) so YottaHost can reproduce results.
4) Data & credentials — Alex will share a small set of sample queries and a staging test account; we need credentials + expected SLAs.

Measurement guidance (please read before building):
- Use stable warm-up period (10 minutes) before recording.
- Report p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end client-observed latency and server-side service time separately.
- Report tokens/sec (aggregate) and per-request token throughput.
- Record KV cache hit-rate and batching stats per run.

Requests for today:
- Marissa: can you drop the run matrix + exact concurrency profiles by EOD?
- Ben: confirm instance types and whether we need quantized images for the test by EOD.
- Jordan: I want a reproducible curl + trace snippet we can hand to Alex.

I attached two files (capacity matrix + probe spec) — please keep this focused and ship a short runnable plan. We'll sync 30m tomorrow if needed.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi — drafted a concrete run matrix below. Attaching the detailed probe doc (p95-p99-probe-spec.md) to this thread and uploading test artifacts to the Drive link.

Proposed run matrix (short):
- Baseline: single-client, seq-len 512, batch-size 1, 1 replica (warm CPU/GPU) — 10k requests
- Long-context: seq-len 2048 and 4096, batch-size 1 & 4, 30m runs each (measure steady-state p95/p99)
- Microburst: M=100 concurrent short requests (seq-len 128) for 10m windows, repeat x3 with 2m cooldown
- KV/Cache probe: run toggles for cold-cache vs warm-cache (measure p99 tail and KV hit-rate)
- Quantization sweep: float16 vs int8 sim (if hyperscalers provide a quantized image)

Metrics to report (per run): p50/p95/p99 client latency, server service time p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec aggregate, per-token compute time, cost-estimate (USD/1M tokens using their posted rates), KV cache hit-rate, batch utilization.

Notes on fairness:
- Use identical model family/checkpoint (they requested we use an open LLM checkpoint that both sides can load). If exact parity isn't possible, document model variance and run a micro-calibration short-run to normalize.
- For batching, measure both continuous batching (Redwood runtime) and naive client-side batching (to mimic hyperscaler behavior).

Schedule suggestion:
- 7/21: provision infra + baseline runs (Ben)
- 7/22: long-context + microburst runs (Marissa + Jordan)
- 7/23: analysis & short readout slide for procurement (Rishi to lead)

I'll post the run YAML and a short harness script to the Drive link tonight.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Performance PM, Redwood Inference

Quick infra note — provisioning plan below. Attaching instance-provision-notes.txt with the exact instance types and startup flags.

Provision plan (staging):
- Redwood baseline: 4x A100 (40GB) with our optimized build (kv-cache enabled, continuous-batching on) — isolated staging pool (dedicated)
- Hyperscaler parity: GCP n1-standard + A100-equivalent GPUs (closest match), Azure NCasT4_v3 or comparable; we'll use their public images where possible.
- Storage: 500GB SSD local for model shards; logging to a central S3 bucket w/ partitioned traces (retain 14 days)

Sizing notes: for microburst tests we may need a 2x headroom buffer on GPU count to avoid queuing artifacts that aren't representative. See attached xlsx for initial numbers.

Question for Marissa/Jordan: do we need to bake a quantized image for int8 testing? If yes I'll queue build — that adds ~4 hours for image bake.

Ben

Adding reproducible artifacts and a few measurement tips. Please include these in the run harness.

1) Trace IDs: add header X-Trace-Id with UUID for every request; persist mapping in the run logs so we can correlate to server spans.

2) Curl repro (minimal):
- curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -H "X-Trace-Id: $TRACE_ID" -d '{"input":"<seed prompt>","max_tokens":512}' https://staging.redwood.internal/v1/generate

3) Logging: capture per-request timings: client-send, tcp-handshake, server-receive, model-start, model-end, server-send. Aggregate to compute p50/p95/p99 server-side.

4) KV cache probe: include a repeat-run where identical prefixes are requested to compute hit-rate. Produce CSV: trace_id, prefix_hash, kv_hit(0/1), server_latency_ms.

5) Seed prompts (examples) — place these in /drive/seeds.txt: short interactive queries, long-context multi-turn prompts, and token-dense completion seeds (math/code).

6) Analysis artifacts: export p95/p99 tables and a small 2-slide summary with key claims + caveats for procurement. Keep the claims conservative and annotate probing parameters.

On quoting Rishi's note below: please ensure we run both client-observed and server-observed latencies — YottaHost will want the end-to-end numbers for procurement.

I'll drop a small harness repo link to the Drive and update the HubSpot record with the lab tasks.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference
